source_text: Ὁ δὲ ἡγεμὼν λέγει τῷ μάρτυρι· Εἰπέ μοι, ἄνθρωπε, πόθεν εἶ, ἢ ποίου γένους τυγχάνεις, ἢ τί τὸ ὄνομά σου; Κόνων εἶπεν· Πόλεως μέν εἰμι ἐγὼ Ναζαρὲθ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, συγγένεια δέ μοί ἐστιν πρὸς Χριστόν, ὃν ἐκ προγόνων λατρεύω, ὃν ἔγνωκα ἐπὶ πάντων θεῶν.
pass_a_gloss: And the governor says to the martyr: Tell me, man, from where are you, or of what stock do you happen to be, or what is your name? Konon said: I am of the city of Nazareth of Galilee, and there is kinship to me toward Christ, whom from forefathers I worship, whom I have known above all gods.
pass_b_english: The governor said to the martyr, Tell me, man, where are you from, and of what lineage are you, and what is your name.
Konon said, I am from the city of Nazareth in Galilee, and I am kin to Christ, whom I worship as handed down from my forefathers, whom I have known as above all gods.

choices.why: τυγχάνω with genitive asks about present status rather than chance, so rendered as a plain question of belonging
rejected: of what race do you happen to be

choices.term: συγγένεια δέ μοί ἐστιν πρὸς Χριστόν
choices.why: dative of possession with εἰμί plus πρός expresses a bond directed toward Christ, not abstract acquaintance
rejected: there is a relationship for me to Christ

choices.why: ἐπί with genitive in comparative context marks superiority over all so-called gods

variants: ἐκ προγόνων λατρεύω: cf. II Tim. 1:3. ἔγνωκα κτλ: cf. Rom. 9:5 (Gebhardt margin).
